# llm-output-leaks-scaffolding-markdown — analysis (generated by analyst on 2026-08-07)

## Problem

LLM-authored replies deliver internal protocol framing to the reader
(v1.1.0 live-test findings F4/F5, reproduced RED on main):

1. Wrapper markers `<<<UNTRUSTED_CONTENT id="…">>>` / `<<<END id="…">>>`
   echoed by the model reach the reader verbatim.
2. Markdown (`**emphasis**`, `---` rules) survives into replies although
   the D30 surface is plain text (`docs/spec/decisions.md:47` — "Plain
   text. Inline code in single backticks; multi-line in triple backticks;
   URLs bare.").

Reproduction verified: `.scratch/M1-779-repro-main.log:4282-4339` —
`M1779ReproProbeIT`, 2 tests / 2 failures against main's `sanitize()`
composition (`applyMarkdownLinkStrip` then `applyClosedListStrip`,
mirrored from `LlmOutputSanitizer.sanitize`,
`infochat-provider/.../llm/LlmOutputSanitizer.java:217-218`): "WRONG
BEHAVIOR ON MAIN: the wrapper opener reached the reader" and "WRONG
BEHAVIOR ON MAIN: markdown emphasis reached the reader". Probe source
parked at `.scratch/M1779ReproProbeIT.java`.

This problem was attempted as M1-779 and abandoned after two redteam
rounds. The prior attempt's diff (`.scratch/M1-779-superseded.diff`) was
green and four of its five round-1 findings were fixed or refuted; the
attempt stopped on one unresolved round-2 finding and on the recognition
(handoff §6) that character-DELETING passes in a shared transform break
postconditions callers assume. This analysis dispositions both.

## Ground truth

Verified against main (all paths repo-relative):

- `LlmOutputSanitizer.sanitize` (infochat-provider/.../llm/LlmOutputSanitizer.java:213-221)
  composes exactly two passes — link strip, then closed-list strip with
  per-token aggregated WARN + `LLM_OUTPUT_SANITIZED` audit rows
  (:236-289). No scaffolding or markdown pass exists.
- The transforms live in **infochat-core**, not infochat-provider:
  `LlmOutputSanitizerCore` (infochat-core/.../core/llm/LlmOutputSanitizerCore.java),
  moved at M1-749; the bean is delegate-only (:36-47 of the bean
  javadoc). **Brief discrepancy:** the brief locates the surface in
  infochat-provider; the transform home is infochat-core.
- `applyClosedListStripWithMatches` (LlmOutputSanitizerCore.java:535-568)
  canonicalizes (NFKC + bidi/zero-width strip, :592-595), re-flattens,
  matches; on zero matches it returns the caller's ORIGINAL bytes
  (:561-562), on any match it returns the CANONICAL form (:567). So a
  representation the raw-byte detectors upstream never saw can be
  synthesized into delivered output today when the same reply also
  carries a closed-list hit (e.g. a leading zero-width space stripped by
  canonicalization moves `[REFUSAL:` to index 0). This is the narrow,
  pre-existing instance of the round-2 mechanism — it makes M1-791's
  reproduction RED today.
- **Caller census (dispositions handoff §6's "~8 call sites" — the real
  count is 13 bean call sites in 8 provider classes plus 1 collector

## Root cause

Fully proven:

1. **Scaffolding leak:** no pass in `sanitize()`'s two-pass composition
   (LlmOutputSanitizer.java:217-218) recognizes the D21 wrapper shape, so
   model-echoed `<<<UNTRUSTED_CONTENT …>>>` / `<<<END …>>>` bytes pass
   through to delivery. Repro: log lines above.
2. **Markdown leak:** same cause for `**` / `---` — D30
   (decisions.md:47) commits the surface to plain text, prompting is
   demonstrably insufficient (design 05:450 already instructs plain
   text), and no enforcement pass exists.
3. **Why the prior attempt kept failing (the meta root cause, handoff
   §6, verified here):** the fix for (1) and (2) is necessarily two
   character-DELETING passes, and deleting characters changes
   postconditions that callers of the shared transform assume but no
   test pins: line count (`DisplayHeadline.derive`:315-322), leading
   bytes (`ChatAgent`:541), token non-synthesis (`stripToolCalls`:1057,
   both two-sided refusal anchors), shrinkage to empty
   (`TranslationPipeline`:455). A green suite proves nothing about
   unpinned assumptions, so each audit round found the next caller by
   inspection. The fix is therefore not "one more remediation round" but
   (a) land each pass with its known caller mitigations, (b) move the
   protocol-token detectors downstream of the deleting passes, and (c)
   run the caller census once, deliberately, as its own ticket.

## Pitfalls

- **P1 — Per-line decomposition DOS (redteam r1 F1, downgraded low,
  fixed shape known).** The new passes are the first line-oriented
  stages; `split("\n", -1)` + per-line `ArrayList`/`StringBuilder`
  converts an in-cap 8 MiB reply into a live-heap multiple of itself.
  §Trust boundaries item 9 (security.md:96-104) puts a hostile
  endpoint's in-cap reply in this input. Both passes must walk lines by
  index into ONE buffer (the prior attempt's rewrite, r2-verified
  closed for live heap). Bites M1-789, M1-790.
- **P2 — A dropped line reaches `DisplayHeadline.derive`'s collapse
  branch (r1 F2).** `derive`'s `lines.length < 2` branch
  (DisplayHeadline.java:316-322) documents exactly one cause — a
  redaction swallowing the separator — and reports the survivor as the
  publisher's own words with `anchored=false`, which
  `ClusterBlockRenderer` promotes and `TranslationPipeline` renders
  UNBRACKETED, breaking D29 (c) from a feed title that flattens to a
  deleted line. Fix (round-1 shipped shape): keep the existing shape
  ONLY when the survivor is EXACTLY `REDACTED_COMMAND_REPLACEMENT`,
  else return `AnchoredHeadline("", "", false)` (the M1-714 omit
  shape). Bites M1-789 (the scaffolding strip is the first line-dropper;
  the fix must land WITH it, not after).
- **P3 — A marker id can swallow a closed-list token out of the audit
  trail (r1 F3a).** `id="[^"]*"` admits `/grant-admin`; the line is then
  deleted before the closed-list pass, no WARN, no row — feed text
  chooses whether the operator's injection-probe signal records a
  privileged token. Fix: the id class excludes `/` (every real id is a
  `UUID.randomUUID()` — r2 re-verified every emitter; every closed-list
  entry begins with `/`). Accepted trade: a command-bearing "marker"
  line RENDERS (redacted) instead of vanishing. Bites M1-789.
- **P4 — A case-sensitive bare-URL guard silently rewrites
  non-lowercase-scheme URLs (r1 F4).** RFC 3986 schemes are
  case-insensitive; `HTTPS://host/a*b*c` must be protected from the
  emphasis deletion exactly like the lowercase spelling, or the pass
  rewrites a link destination. Fix: `(?i:https?)://\S+` in the verbatim
  span. Bites M1-790.
- **P5 — Character-joining passes synthesize protocol tokens PAST
  detectors that run on raw text upstream of `sanitize()` (r2
  INFO-LEAK/medium, UNRESOLVED — carried forward, not retired).**
  Emphasis deletion joins `[REFUS**AL**:` → `[REFUSAL:` and
  `TOOL_C**A**LL:` → `TOOL_CALL:`; a dropped leading line moves an
  already-contiguous `[REFUSAL:` to index 0. The four detectors
  (ChatAgent.java:541, ChatAgent.java:520/:1057,
  CategoryRollupGenerator.java:203, SummaryProseGenerator.java:128) all
  run BEFORE sanitize, and ChatAgent's own soundness argument (:534-536)
  holds only for deleting passes placed BEFORE the check. The
  closed-list half of the same mechanism is already covered by pass
  ordering (`/b**a**n` → `/ban` is re-scanned because the downgrade runs
  before the closed-list strip — r1 F4 refutation leg). Verified
  pre-existing narrow instance (zero-width prefix + any closed-list hit
  → canonical form returned with `[REFUSAL:` at index 0,
  LlmOutputSanitizerCore.java:536,561-567) makes this RED today.
  Correction carried from the handoff (§5): the `---\n[REFUSAL:` half is
  a PRE-EXISTING prefix-only-matching weakness, not a regression —
  pre-diff the delivered bytes already contained the marker. The
  genuinely new capability is FRAGMENT SYNTHESIS. Fix: M1-791 moves the
  detectors to evaluate the sanitized text; M1-790 is blocked on M1-791.
- **P6 — "Blank instead of drop" is a rejected fix shape (handoff
  §3.2).** Blanking a deleted line preserves line count but yields
  `lines[1] == ""` → `AnchoredHeadline(anchor, "", true)` → an EMPTY
  primary line, contradicts the §Expected rendering, and does nothing
  for P5. Do not "fix" P2 this way.
- **P7 — `contains` instead of exact equality in the P2 fix hands the
  leak back.** `[redacted command]` is forgeable from a prompt-injected
  `title_en`; `contains` admits attacker prose riding alongside the
  forgery, exact equality can only ever deliver the fixed literal.
- **P8 — `sanitize()` can return "" for a non-empty reply (r1
  out-of-model 1, widened by r2; RECORDED RESIDUAL, dispositioned not
  fixed here).** A markers-only / breaks-only reply now reduces to
  nothing; `TranslationPipeline.java:454-455` promises non-empty for
  non-empty input, the display-hit cache (:560) would store the empty
  value for 24h, and no empty-body guard exists at OutboundDelivery. The
  round-1 disposition (a delivery-path guard is outside the sanitizer
  ticket) stands; M1-792's census names the follow-up explicitly.
- **P9 — CRLF endpoints defeat line-shape matching (r2 out-of-model).**
  A trailing `\r` reads as content, so a thematic-break line is not
  dropped and an opened fence never closes — under-delivery only, but
  the spec sentence "a thematic-break line is dropped" is stated
  unconditionally. M1-790 must either tolerate `\r` (chosen — cheap, and
  keeps the sentence absolute) or scope the sentence.
- **P10 — security.md is parity-gated.** Amendments must not introduce
  an `infochat.*` token without a real `@ConfigProperty` or a ledger
  exemption (handoff §8; engineering-rules §8 documented-key rule).
  Bites M1-789, M1-790, M1-791.
- **P11 — The closed list is frozen.** `matchSetEqualsSpecClosedList`
  (:871) pins CLOSED_LIST against commands.md; adding/removing/reordering
  an entry is out of scope for every ticket here (M1-779 out_of_scope,
  carried forward).
- **P12 — M1-778 collision.** M1-778 (pending) owns `ChatAgent.java` and
  `TranslationPipeline.java`; M1-791 must be `blocked_by: [M1-778]`.
  Also: M1-778's design calls `DisplayHeadline.displaysAsTheOriginal` /
  `usesAnchor` — neither predicate's semantics may move (handoff §8);
  only the private `derive` collapse branch changes, in M1-789.
- **P13 — Do not rewire `IngestTranslationWorker`** (:775-777) to the
  new passes: stored-corpus change with its own cost, colliding with
  M1-776; translator output already reaches readers through the render
  sites (M1-779 out_of_scope, carried forward).
- **P14 — Audit-count preservation.** Every token that matched before
  the new passes must still match and row. Known accepted residual
  (r1 F3b, r2-corrected): emphasis deletion can SPLIT a token
  (`/ban*x*` → `/banx`), losing a row a pre-diff match produced — closed
  because the residue is never dispatchable (the trailing lookahead at
  LlmOutputSanitizerCore's closed-list pattern rejects it), NOT because
  the link strip could do the same (it only adds separators — r2's
  correction; carry the corrected reasoning, not the round-1 leg).
- **P15 — NFKC canonical-form residual.** On a closed-list match the
  canonical form is returned (:567), which can re-surface emphasis or
  marker bytes the raw-byte passes never saw — cosmetic, in a reply that
  also carried a redacted command; closing it would mean a deleting pass
  after the redaction (forbidden by the ordering rule). The amendment
  must state this residual, as the prior attempt's did.
- **P16 — Sibling fixture calibration.** M1-789 must not pin, by test or
  spec sentence, any behavior M1-790 is mandated to change (e.g. that
  `**`/`---` survive): the parked probe is restored per-METHOD (789
  restores the scaffolding method, 790 the markdown method), and 789's
  security.md amendment covers the scaffolding category only. M1-791
  lands BEFORE M1-790, so its failure-mode tests must use today's
  synthesis route (zero-width + closed-list hit), not 790's emphasis
  pass.

## Solution options

- **A — Re-run M1-779 as one ticket** (both passes + all mitigations,
  one diff). Rejected: this is the exact shape that looped for two
  redteam rounds; handoff §6 shows the loop terminates only when an
  auditor runs out of callers to notice.
- **B — Scaffolding strip only, drop the markdown downgrade
  permanently.** Rejected as a sole plan: F5 stays unfixed while
  readers keep receiving `**`/`---`. Adopted as the decomposition
  BOUNDARY instead — the marker strip is the far less reactive half and
  can land first.
- **C — Four-ticket decomposition (chosen).** 789 scaffolding strip +
  the P2 derive fix; 790 markdown downgrade, blocked on 789 (same
  files) and 791 (P5); 791 protocol-token detectors moved
  post-sanitize, blocked on M1-778 (P12); 792 caller-postcondition
  census + pinning tests + named follow-ups (P8, TranslationPipeline
  (b)/(c)). Each ticket carries its known mitigations; the dependency
  edges encode the order the redteam record proves necessary.
- **D — Neutralize `[REFUSAL:`/`TOOL_CALL:` inside the sanitizer**
  (handoff option 2). Rejected: it ships the reply with a neutralized
  token instead of taking the degrade paths the three call sites promise
  (bundle string + null commit; `Optional.empty()`; degraded prose) —
  strictly weaker than C/791.
- **E — Disposition P5 as a stated residual** (handoff option 3).
  Rejected: the fragment-synthesis half is verified new against main
  (Ground truth, LlmOutputSanitizerCore.java:536,561-567), and shipping
  M1-790 over an unmoved detector set would re-enter the audit loop with
  a known-live mechanism.

## Chosen approach

Option C. Derivation per decision:

- The strip categories implement security.md §LLM output sanitizer's
  "full set of LLM-authored output surfaces" (security.md:357-359) read
  together with D30's plain-text commitment (decisions.md:47) and the
  §Prompt-injection defenses scaffolding-confidentiality posture
  (security.md:303-310); each ticket amends §LLM output sanitizer to
  record its category (M1-779 precedent: the amendment rides the same
  diff, parity gates respected per P10).
- The transforms go in `LlmOutputSanitizerCore` (M1-749's single-home
  rule), reached through the bean's static-delegate shape; `sanitize()`
  composes them BEFORE the closed-list strip (the ordering rule the
  prior amendment wrote and r2 verified: every DELETING pass runs before
  the redaction, none after; `breakLinkAdjacency` only inserts a space).
- 789 = new `applyScaffoldingMarkerStrip` (index-walk per P1, id class
  excludes `/` per P3, marker-only line dropped per the M1-779 §Expected
  rendering) + the P2 exact-equality fix in `DisplayHeadline.derive`
  (P6/P7 guard the shape) + spec amendment (scaffolding category +
  collapsed-pair rule).
- 790 = new `applyPlainTextDowngrade` (emphasis per CommonMark flanking,
  thematic-break line dropped — CRLF-tolerant per P9, list marker →
  `· `, fence-aware, scheme-case-insensitive URL guard per P4,
  index-walk per P1) + spec amendment (markdown category, fence scope
  "by this pass", P14/P15 residuals stated).
- 791 = the four P5 detectors evaluate the sanitized text (degrade paths
  byte-identical), implementing §Prompt-injection defenses' refusal
  contract on the text actually delivered; `blocked_by: [M1-778]` (P12).
- 792 = the handoff §6 census, once: the 13 bean call sites + 1
  collector composition enumerated above, each with its assumed
  postconditions recorded and pinned by a test where unpinned; files the
  P8 and TranslationPipeline-(b)/(c) follow-ups. Not a blocker for
  789/790/791: the redteam record already enumerated those tickets'
  caller assumptions; 792 is the systematic backstop, and gating
  everything on it re-creates the stall the user stopped.
- Implementation order: 789 now; 792 anytime (recommended right after
  789 so the census reflects the new pass); 791 after M1-778 lands; 790
  after 789 + 791.

## Controls to preserve (engineering-rules §10)

For every path the change reroutes or re-parameterizes:

- The closed-list strip, its canonical-form matching, per-token
  aggregated WARN, and `LLM_OUTPUT_SANITIZED` audit rows
  (LlmOutputSanitizer.java:168-179, :236-289) — same path, same unit
  (one author's field or its ingest pair). New passes run BEFORE it;
  P14 names the one accepted row-loss residual.
- The `](`-free outbound guarantee (OutboundDelivery.java:219/:232/:265)
  — untouched; the new passes run upstream of it.
- The pair-as-ONE-sanitize-call unit (DisplayHeadline.java:311-314) —
  splitting it into two calls is not an acceptable fix (M1-697 control).
- The four straddling-redaction tests (Ground truth list) — not one
  assertion edited; exact equality in the P2 fix is what preserves them
  (the broader "omit on any collapse" rule was run and failed all four,
  handoff §3.2).
- `matchSetEqualsSpecClosedList` (:871) and the closed list (P11).
- `adversarialFlagScanIsLinearNotQuadratic` (:553) and the r1-added
  3s-bounded walk test pattern — P1's regression gate.
- The degrade paths the P5 detectors trigger: ChatAgent's bundle string
  + null commit (:542-545), CategoryRollupGenerator's `Optional.empty()`
  (:209-210), SummaryProseGenerator's degraded prose (:135-137) — M1-791
  moves the trigger's OPERAND, never the consequence.
- Renderer-side re-sanitization of `ClusterProse` bytes
  (ClusterBlockRenderer.java:183, DigestRenderer.java:610/:881) — kept
  even when M1-791 also sanitizes at generation: renderers never trust
  the bytes a hand-assembled record carries (redteam 2026-07-25).
- `displaysAsTheOriginal` / `usesAnchor` semantics (P12).

## Verification strategy

Every pitfall maps to a named test in the owning ticket (each ticket's
Verification section carries the mapping). Headlines:

- P1 → per-pass many-line walk tests under a time bound (789, 790).
- P2 → `DisplayHeadlineTest`: a feed title flattening to a droppable
  line cannot put the anchor in the `originalLine` slot (789).
- P3 → audit IT: `<<<END id="/grant-admin">>>` is redacted AND rowed
  (789, failure-mode).
- P4 → `HTTPS://…/a*b*c` survives unrewritten (790, failure-mode).
- P5 → 791: the zero-width + closed-list-hit synthesis route degrades
  the turn / yields no roll-up / degrades the cluster (RED today);
  790: `/b**a**n` is re-scanned, redacted, and audited (failure-mode).
- P7 → forged-marker test: attacker text appended to a forged
  `[redacted command]` does not buy the leak back (789, failure-mode).
- P9 → CRLF thematic-break test (790).
- P8, TranslationPipeline (b)/(c) → follow-up tickets filed by 792;
  census pinning tests assert the documented postconditions honestly
  (including that "" is a possible return today, so the follow-up is
  not silently closed by a pinning test).
- Every ticket: `mvn -B -pl infochat-provider -am verify` green with
  ALL preserved tests unchanged.

## Decomposition

1. **M1-789 — strip scaffolding markers** (independent). 6 files:
   LlmOutputSanitizerCore.java, LlmOutputSanitizer.java,
   LlmOutputSanitizerTest.java, DisplayHeadline.java,
   DisplayHeadlineTest.java, docs/spec/security.md.
2. **M1-792 — caller postcondition census** (independent; recommended
   second). Census doc + pinning tests + 2 follow-up tickets.
3. **M1-791 — post-sanitize upstream detectors**
   (`blocked_by: [M1-778]`). ChatAgent.java,
   CategoryRollupGenerator.java, SummaryProseGenerator.java + tests.
4. **M1-790 — downgrade markdown** (`blocked_by: [M1-789, M1-791]`).
   LlmOutputSanitizerCore.java, LlmOutputSanitizer.java,
   LlmOutputSanitizerTest.java, docs/spec/security.md.

## SPEC-GAP

None. The spec supports the solution: §LLM output sanitizer already
commits the sanitizer to the full set of LLM-authored surfaces and D30
commits the plain-text surface; recording new strip categories is an
amendment riding each ticket's diff (M1-779 precedent), not a change to
what the spec promises. The P8 empty-string and TranslationPipeline
(b)/(c) items are defect follow-ups within the existing spec text
(llm.md §Failure handling conditions b/c; TranslationPipeline.java:455
documents its own contract), not spec changes.
